alerts.title: Abdominal pain may relate to TDF toxicity
alerts.message: Guidelines list abdominal pain or discomfort and decreased appetite as presenting signs of TDF toxicity, including lactic acidosis or severe hepatomegaly with steatosis. The patient reports abdominal pain while on TDF-containing regimen (TLD) since March 2023. Appetite is preserved and no fever is present, which argues against an infectious cause. However, TDF-associated lactic acidosis can present with abdominal pain even with normal appetite. Evidence against drug attribution includes the absence of exhaustion, muscle cramps, or headache, and normal creatinine (82 umol/L). LFTs have not been checked to exclude hepatic involvement.

evidence.recommended_action: Perform LFTs and RFTs as guidelines recommend for suspected TDF toxicity. If liver enzymes are elevated or eGFR <60, substitute TDF with ABC.

alerts.title: LFTs not ordered for abdominal pain on TDF
alerts.message: Guidelines state that for TDF toxicity presenting with abdominal pain or discomfort, clinicians should perform LFTs and RFTs, and if deranged, substitute TDF with ABC. The patient's creatinine was checked 78 days ago and is normal (82 umol/L). However, no liver function tests have been ordered despite the complaint of abdominal pain. The clinician's plan documents the symptom but does not include any laboratory evaluation. This is a monitoring gap given the guideline recommendation to investigate abdominal pain in patients on TDF.

evidence.recommended_action: Order LFTs (ALT/AST) to evaluate abdominal pain in the context of TDF therapy. Also repeat creatinine/eGFR as part of the toxicity workup.

alerts.title: Low-level viremia at 25 copies/mL needs attention
alerts.message: Guidelines define viral suppression as VL <200 copies/mL for plasma samples. The patient's VL of 25 copies/mL is suppressed. However, guidelines acknowledge low-level viremia as a risk for subsequent virologic non-suppression and treatment failure. The patient has been on TLD since March 2023, approximately 34 months. The VL was done 78 days before the current visit. No repeat VL or enhanced adherence support is mentioned in the plan, though the value is well below the suppression threshold.

evidence.recommended_action: Continue routine VL monitoring every 12 months as the patient is suppressed. Consider enhanced adherence counseling given detectable low-level viremia.

Facilities should constitute a multidisciplinary VL review committees to review, track, and make decisions to optimize ART regimen by switching to second-line, third- line, or a more potent regimen.
